study.question: Does the observed terminal matching gain require task-query-dependent field selection, or does a uniform same-field match prior suffice? Does correct alignment of those matches with history events account for the gain? R4 terminal-only macro AUC0.819232531 exceeds off0.811178251 and joint0.812356527; internal-only0.804323157 is worse. These are single-seed observations, not established mechanisms. The terminal-only versus off gain is largest in history>64 (0.012129975) and smaller at1..16 (0.001895924); empty-history differences cannot be caused by inference-time matching and flag shared-training effects.
study.hypothesis: A terminal-only uniform mixture of the five exact same-field target/history indicators can retain or improve the incumbent by providing stable event alignment without coupling this explicit prior to evolving task queries. Correct event alignment, rather than an arbitrary bounded attention offset with the same per-sample match-count distribution, explains most of the useful signal. This is a falsifiable simplification of the current mechanism, not a novelty claim or an assumption that general adaptive sequence retrieval is unnecessary.

study.proposed_difference: Prospective2x2 replacement: uniform versus adaptive terminal field weights, crossed with aligned versus within-sample valid-event-rotated match channels. Candidate terminal_uniform sets every match-field weight to1/5, so terminal bias=2*mean(binary matches). terminal_adaptive reproduces the parent endpoint. Rotation packs only valid rows, cyclically shifts all five channels together by max(1,floor(valid_count/2)), then restores the original mask positions, leaving event keys/values/order and target tokens unchanged. At fixed queries/parameters it preserves the full prior histogram and cross-field co-occurrence multiset while disrupting its event alignment for nontrivial histories. All arms compute both field selectors and rotation, add no parameters, keep global history support, and leave intermediate matching disabled. No local training or new measured model result is produced in this phase.
predictions: Aligned uniform macro AUC will be at least competitive with aligned adaptive; a higher score under the frozen exact selection rule supports choosing the simpler prior. A near tie is descriptive, not statistical equivalence.

Both aligned arms should exceed their rotated counterparts, especially for history>64; define alignment effects U_aligned-U_rotated and A_aligned-A_rotated, and their difference-in-differences. Positive alignment effects support event-specific matching only for the tested implementation.

At identical parameters, aligned adaptive predictions and gradients must agree with the supplied parent within FP32 atol1e-6/rtol1e-5 and BF16 atol/rtol1e-2, allowing host-documented sparse gradient handling. Match interventions must have no forward effect on empty histories at shared parameters; trained empty-history metrics can differ.

Expected total parameter count32115012 and embedding count31793216 are inherited unchanged; actual host counts and whole-run/inference costs must confirm capacity and cost. No efficiency gain is claimed from the matched-computation implementation.

Report every task AUC/Logloss and deltas versus baseline-din and the parent, macro Logloss, parameters, train/inference seconds and latency. Preserve existing history bins empty,1..16,17..64,>64 and report samples/positive/negative counts; flag task slices with fewer than20 positives or20 negatives or200 samples as insufficient for firm inference. No bootstrap intervals, match-pattern slices or other unavailable diagnostics may be invented. Equal-pass contrasts do not establish equal-compute efficiency.
falsifiers: A reproducible adaptive-over-uniform advantage rejects the proposed selector simplification, even if uniform still improves on historical match-off.

Aligned and rotated arms perform similarly or rotation improves across paired repetitions: the present study then fails to attribute the gain to event alignment; shared regularization, recency disruption or optimization remain explanations.

Parent endpoint parity, finite forward/backward, parameter shape matching, masking invariance, or per-channel rotation-count invariance fails: repair before host training and retain any consumed failed-attempt cost. Do not interpret a failed execution as scientific counterevidence.
History-length patterns fail to repeat or a few rare-label slices dominate; qualify the hypothesis rather than changing bins or task weights after observing results.
alternative_explanations: Separate training trajectories change learned queries and embeddings; same shapes do not imply equal effective function classes.

A deterministic half-history rotation disrupts both content and recency association; periodic or constant match channels and histories of length0/1 can be unchanged. It is not independent randomization or proof that every match is removed.

Uniform weights change field mixture, gradient routes and prior distribution jointly; the selector effect is conditional on this explicit prior, not an isolated claim about general adaptive retrieval.
One original training seed and repeated validation selection leave initialization and selection uncertainty.
Target category/brand repetition is closely related to auxiliary label construction; improvements may reflect this offline benchmark rather than production-time causal validity.

These reject those implementations locally, not all future feedback/routing mechanisms. No executed failure is reported in supplied receipts and previous_runtime_error is null.
